30 kg/m2, whichever represents the lower weight. For
example, it is possible for an adolescent to have a BMI
30 kg/m2 but have a BMI-for-age that is  95th percen-
tile, in which case the adolescent would still be classiﬁ ed 
as obese. The BMI of an adolescent is classiﬁ ed as obese 
when it is 30 kg/m2 even if it is  95th percentile curve.3–5
